# Parse old_songs entries from the file content
import re

content = old_songs_file['content']
lines = content.strip().split('\n')
# Skip the first line "# Archived Songs"
old_songs = []
for line in lines[1:]:
    line = line.strip()
    if not line:
        continue
    # Format: "- Title by Artist1, Artist2"
    # Remove leading "- "
    if line.startswith('- '):
        line = line[2:]
    # Split on " by " (case sensitive? we'll use regex)
    # The pattern: title by artists
    m = re.match(r'^(.*?)\s+by\s+(.+)$', line)
    if m:
        title = m.group(1).strip()
        artists_str = m.group(2).strip()
        # Split artists by comma
        artists = [a.strip() for a in artists_str.split(',')]
        old_songs.append({'title': title, 'artists': artists})
    else:
        print("Could not parse line:", line)

print("Parsed old songs:")
for s in old_songs:
    print(s)

# Collect all unique song IDs from all playlists
all_song_ids = set()
for pl in all_playlists:

print("Unique song IDs:", sorted(all_song_ids))

# Match songs against old_songs list

for s in old_songs:

            expected_artists = [a.lower() for a in song['artists']]

# Search for all 18 songs and collect their song_ids
archive_song_ids = []
for song in songs_to_archive:
    query = song["title"] + " " + song["artist"]
    results = apis.spotify.search_songs(query=query, access_token=login_result["access_token"])
    # Find exact match
    found = None
    for r in results:
        if r["title"] == song["title"] and any(a["name"] == song["artist"] for a in r["artists"]):
            found = r["song_id"]
            break
    if found is not None:
        archive_song_ids.append(found)
        print(f"Found: {song['title']} by {song['artist']} -> song_id {found}")

            songs_to_archive.append({'title': title.strip(), 'artist': artist.strip()})

# Parse the old songs list from the file content
old_songs_content = """# List of Songs to Archive
- City of Fallen Angels by Hazel Winter
- Sacred Ground by Noah Bennett
- Echoes from the Abyss by Noah Bennett
- Beneath the Surface of Love by Velvet Echo
- Lost in the Maze of Your Mind by Noah Bennett
- Crimson Veil by Phoenix Rivers
- In the Wake of Goodbye by Lucas Grey
- The Puzzle of My Heart by Jasper Skye, Isabella Cruz, Seraphina Dawn
- A Broken Heart's Lament by Lucas Diaz
- Whispers of a Forgotten Love by Lily Moon, Zoey James
- Strangers Again by Oceanic Odyssey
- When Dawn Breaks Without You by Lucas Grey
- Secrets of the Heart by Carter Knight
"""

old_songs = []
for line in old_songs_content.strip().splitlines():
    line = line.strip()
    if line.startswith("- "):
        line = line[2:]
        if " by " in line:
            title, artists_str = line.split(" by ", 1)
            artists = [a.strip() for a in artists_str.split(",")]
            old_songs.append((title.strip(), artists))
        else:
            # no artists? skip or handle
            pass

print("Old songs parsed:")
for t, a in old_songs:
    print(f"  {t} by {a}")

song_ids = {}

for song in songs_to_archive[1:]:
    title = song['title']
    artists = song['artists']
    # Search by title
    results = apis.spotify.search_songs(query=title, access_token=access_token)
    # Find matching song
    found = None
    for r in results:
        if r['title'] == title:
            # Check if any artist matches
            r_artist_names = [a['name'] for a in r['artists']]
            if any(artist in r_artist_names for artist in artists):
                found = r['song_id']
                break
    if found:
        song_ids[title] = found
        print(f"Found: {title} -> {found}")
    else:
        print(f"NOT FOUND: {title}")

print("All song_ids:", song_ids)

    'Trapped in a Daydream': '04/2021',
    'Mystic Voyage to Avalon': '08/2020'
}

new_lines = []
for line in lines:

        # Extract song title: format "- <title> BY <artists> RELEASED_AT TODO"

        parts = line.split(' BY ')

        # title_part is the song title
        if title_part in release_map:
            new_line = line.replace('TODO', release_map[title_part])
            new_lines.append(new_line)
        else:
            new_lines.append(line)  # keep as is if not found
    else:
        new_lines.append(line)

        date = release_dates.get(song_title)
        if date:

        else:

    new_lines.append(line)

print(new_content)

        parts = line.strip()[2:].split(' BY ')

# Search for all TODO songs and collect their release dates
import re

# Parse song titles from todo lines
songs_to_search = []
for line in todo_lines:
    # Extract title: between "- " and " BY "
    match = re.match(r"- (.+?) BY (.+?) RELEASED_AT TODO", line)
    if match:
        title = match.group(1)
        artists = match.group(2)
        songs_to_search.append((title, artists, line))

# We'll search each and store release month/year
release_map = {}
for title, artists, line in songs_to_search:
    # Search with title and artist to narrow
    query = f"{title} {artists.split(',')[0].strip()}"
    result = apis.spotify.search_songs(query=query, access_token=spotify_token, page_limit=1)
    if result:
        # Find the song that matches title exactly
        song = None
        for s in result:
            if s['title'].lower() == title.lower():
                song = s
                break
        if song:
            release_date = song['release_date']
            # Extract month/year
            month = release_date[5:7]
            year = release_date[:4]
            release_map[line] = f"RELEASED_AT {month}/{year}"
            print(f"Found: {title} -> {month}/{year}")
        else:
            print(f"No exact match for {title}")
    else:
        print(f"No result for {title}")

print("Done searching")

# Build mapping from song title to release month/year
from datetime import datetime

# release_dates dict from previous step: song_id -> release_date string
# We need to map title to release date. We have song info from show_song, but we didn't store titles.
# Let's re-fetch song info for each ID to get title and release date, or we can use the search results we already have.
# We have search results for "When All Words Fail Us" and "Final Echo" which gave us song IDs and release dates.
# For the others, we have release_dates dict with song_id -> release_date, but we need titles.
# We can use the liked_songs list which has song_id and title, but not release_date.
# We'll fetch each song's info again to get title and release_date together.

# Actually we already have release_dates dict with song_id -> release_date, and we have liked_songs list with song_id -> title.
# Let's create a mapping from song_id to title from liked_songs.
liked_songs = apis.spotify.show_liked_songs(access_token=spotify_token, page_index=0, page_limit=20)
title_by_id = {song['song_id']: song['title'] for song in liked_songs}

# Now create mapping from title to release month/year
release_month_year = {}
for sid, date_str in release_dates.items():
    title = title_by_id.get(sid)
    if title:
        # Parse date string to get month and year
        dt = datetime.fromisoformat(date_str.replace('Z', '+00:00'))
        month_year = f"{dt.month:02d}/{dt.year}"
        release_month_year[title] = month_year

print(release_month_year)

# Now I'll update the note content with all release dates.
# Build mapping from song title to release month/year
release_dates = {
    "Silver Lining": "12/2022",
    "Walking Through the Valley of Shadows": "08/2022",
    "Where Shadows Come to Life": "01/2023",
    "Eternal Melancholy": "04/2023",
    "Crimson Veil": "01/2020",
    "Elusive Joy": "03/2021",
    "Ephemeral Beauty": "01/2020",
    "Stardust Serenade": "04/2019",
    "Veiled Behind a Mask of Joy": "10/2022",
    "In the Wake of Unspoken Promises": "07/2022",
    "Wading Through the Ashes of Love": "09/2020",
    "Fading Like a Distant Star": "01/2019",
    "Wilted Grace": "01/2022",
}

content = _mem['s14']['content']
lines = content.split('\n')
new_lines = []
for line in lines:
    if 'RELEASED_AT TODO' in line:
        # Extract song title: line starts with "- " and has " BY " before artist
        # e.g. "- Silver Lining BY Ava Morgan RELEASED_AT TODO"
        # Find the part between "- " and " BY "
        title = line.split('- ')[1].split(' BY ')[0].strip()
        if title in release_dates:
            line = line.replace('RELEASED_AT TODO', f"RELEASED_AT {release_dates[title]}")
        else:
            print(f"Warning: no release date for {title}")
    new_lines.append(line)
new_content = '\n'.join(new_lines)
print(new_content)

        # Split by " BY " to get title part
        parts = line.split(' BY ')

            if title_part.startswith('- '):

# Now I'll update the note content, replacing each TODO with the correct release date.

content = note['content']

# Mapping of song title to release month/year
release_dates = {
    "Silver Lining": "12/2022",
    "Walking Through the Valley of Shadows": "08/2022",
    "Where Shadows Come to Life": "01/2023",
    "Eternal Melancholy": "04/2023",
    "Crimson Veil": "01/2020",

    "Ephemeral Beauty": "01/2020",
    "Stardust Serenade": "04/2019",
    "Veiled Behind a Mask of Joy": "10/2022",
    "In the Wake of Unspoken Promises": "07/2022",
    "Wading Through the Ashes of Love": "09/2020",
    "Fading Like a Distant Star": "01/2019",
    "Wilted Grace": "01/2022"
}

# Split content into lines and replace TODO for each song
lines = content.split('\n')
new_lines = []
for line in lines:
    if 'RELEASED_AT TODO' in line:
        # Extract song title from the line: format "- Song Title BY Artist RELEASED_AT TODO"
        # The song title is between "- " and " BY "
        song_title = line.split(' BY ')[0].lstrip('- ').strip()
        if song_title in release_dates:
            line = line.replace('RELEASED_AT TODO', f'RELEASED_AT {release_dates[song_title]}')
    new_lines.append(line)

new_content = '\n'.join(new_lines)

# Update the note with the new content
print(apis.simple_note.update_note(note_id=3084, access_token=access_token, content=new_content))

# Get liked songs (first page)
print(apis.spotify.show_liked_songs(access_token=access_token, page_index=0, page_limit=20))

# Get all liked songs (handle pagination)
liked_songs = []
page_index = 0
while True:
    page = apis.spotify.show_liked_songs(access_token=access_token, page_index=page_index, page_limit=20)
    liked_songs.extend(page)
    if len(page) < 20:
        break
    page_index += 1

# Get current queue
queue = apis.spotify.show_song_queue(access_token=access_token)

# Build set of liked song IDs
liked_ids = {song['song_id'] for song in liked_songs}

# Find positions of liked songs in queue
positions_to_remove = [song['position'] for song in queue if song['song_id'] in liked_ids]

# Remove from highest position to lowest to avoid shifting issues
positions_to_remove.sort(reverse=True)
print("Positions to remove:", positions_to_remove)

# Remove liked songs from queue (descending order to avoid index shifts)
for pos in positions_to_remove:
    result = apis.spotify.remove_song_from_queue(position=pos, access_token=access_token)
    print(f"Removed position {pos}: {result}")

# Check the play_music API documentation
print(apis.api_docs.show_api_doc(app_name='spotify', api_name='play_music'))

# Start the player (play current song in queue)
result = apis.spotify.play_music(access_token=access_token)
print(result)
